title: Preprocessor Phases
concept: The preprocessor expands macros and directives before compilation to create the actual compiled code.

steps.title: Preprocessor directive: #include
steps.explanation: **`#include <stdio.h>`** — Code starting with `#` is a directive for the **Preprocessor**. Preprocessing occurs **earlier** than compilation, and involves finding the `stdio.h` file on the system path and copying its **entire contents (thousands of lines)** to this location.

steps.title: Preprocessor directive: #define (macro constant)
steps.explanation: **`#define PI 3.14159`** — Defines a **macro constant** called `PI`. The preprocessor makes a **simple text substitution** of `3.14159` whenever it encounters `PI` in subsequent code.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: **`int main() {`** — The program entry point where the compiler begins reading the code after preprocessing has finished. At this point, the contents of `stdio.h` have already been inserted, and all `PI` and `HELLO` have been replaced with their actual values.

steps.title: Execute after macro substitution (string)
steps.explanation: **`printf("%s\n", HELLO);`** — When the compiler looks at this code, `HELLO` has already been replaced with `"Hello, World!"`, so it is actually 100% identical to `printf("%s\n", "Hello, World!");`.

steps.title: variable declaration
steps.explanation: **`double r = 10.0;`** — Create radius `r` in **stack memory** and initialize it to `10.0`. `double` is an 8-byte floating point type that can represent up to approximately 15 decimal places.

steps.title: Execute after macro substitution (number)
steps.explanation: **`double area = PI * r * r;`** — To the compiler, it appears as `double area = 3.14159 * r * r;`. `3.14159 * 10.0 * 10.0` = `314.159` is calculated and stored in a new variable `area`.

steps.title: Result output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Area: %.2f\n", area);`** — Prints the area of ​​the circle to **2 decimal places**. In `%.2f`, `.2` means display only up to 2 decimal places, and the third digit `9` is rounded off to output `314.16`.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
**`return 0;`** — An exit code that signals "normal completion" to the operating system.

The key point of this lesson is that **the preprocessor is a separate entity from the compiler**.

quiz.question: Can I get the memory address of a constant defined with #define MAX 100 with &MAX?
options: It's impossible. There is no address because it is replaced with a number before compilation.
This is possible by turning on certain options.
There is an address in the stack area.
quiz.explanation: The macro constant `#define` changes the text of the source code to its value at the preprocessor stage, so it does not exist as a variable at runtime.

misconceptions.correct:
It's completely different.
Variables take up memory space, but macros are just text substitutions in the source code.
misconceptions.why: The text is changed unconditionally without checking the type.

keyTakeaway: The preprocessor is the step that transforms the 'code text' itself before the compiler sees the code.
